name: peg (rust-peg)
description: PEG parser generator via a procedural macro DSL embedded in Rust

approach.comment: Per Assessment Guidelines: PEG grammar written inside the `peg::parser!{ grammar NAME() for INPUT { ... } }` proc-macro block, expanded at compile time into a Rust module.

implementation.comment: peg -> peg-macros (proc-macro2, quote) + peg-runtime (zero deps). No C/C++ anywhere in the tree.

crates-io.comment: `peg` is the umbrella crate re-exporting `peg-macros` (proc-macro) and `peg-runtime` (traits, ParseError); all three are released in lockstep.

documentation.comment: No separate book; the crate-level rustdoc is the grammar syntax reference.

grammar-class.comment: Parsing expression grammar: ordered choice `/`, `&`/`!` lookahead, optional packrat memoisation via `#[cache]`.

grammar-definition.comment: Grammar lives inside `peg::parser!{}` in the Rust source; action blocks are ordinary Rust expressions.

left-recursion.comment: `#[cache_left_rec]` (since 0.8.0) 'extends the #[cache] mechanism with the ability to resolve left-recursive rules, which are otherwise an error'; `precedence!{}` implements precedence climbing for infix/prefix/postfix operators. Guideline: PEG tools get native only when left recursion is documented, which it is here.

ambiguity-handling.comment: `e1 / e2 / e3` tries alternatives in order and commits to the first match (PEG semantics).

backtracking.comment: Failed alternatives and `{? }` conditional actions backtrack freely; no cut/commit operator in the grammar syntax.

lexer-integration.comment: Scannerless over `&str`/`&[u8]` by default; a grammar declared `for [Token]` parses any token slice with `[Token::Variant(x)]` patterns, so a separate lexer (e.g. logos) can be used.

precedence-pratt-support.comment: `precedence!{ ... }` block with `@` operand markers and `--` level separators (precedence climbing).

unicode-aware.comment: `str` input's `parse_elem` yields `char` and advances by `len_utf8()`; `[..]` patterns match chars; `LineCol` columns are counted in chars.

input-types.comment: Built-in impls for `str`, `[u8]`, and generic `[T]`; custom inputs implement `Parse`/`ParseElem`/`ParseLiteral`/`ParseSlice`.

streaming-partial-input.comment: README comparison table: 'Streaming input: No'. `#[no_eof]` only allows prefix matching of complete input.

zero-copy.comment: `$(e)` returns the matched slice of the input (`&'input str` / `&'input [T]`); test `borrow_from_input.rs` covers ASTs borrowing from input.

span-tracking.comment: `position!()` yields a `usize` byte offset; `inject name(input, lpos, rpos)` (0.8.6) auto-computes start/end offsets for every action block. `ParseError<LineCol>` for str input carries line, column, and byte offset. Custom inputs choose their own `PositionRepr`.

output-model.comment: Each rule declares a Rust return type and builds it in its action block; no generic tree.

semantic-actions.comment: `a:e1 b:e2 { rust }` actions and `{? rust }` fallible conditional actions (`Result<T, &str>`).

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: No implicit skipping: whitespace is an ordinary rule the user writes and references explicitly (docs: `_`/`__` rules 'conventionally used to match whitespace between tokens').

stateful-parsing.comment: Grammar-level arguments (`grammar lol(config: bool) for str`) are visible in every rule; rules also take value/type/`rule<T>` parameters.

error-recovery.comment: Parse returns `Err(ParseError)` at the furthest failure position; no sync/skip or recovery API.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: Single `ParseError` (one location + expected set) per run.

expected-token-reporting.comment: `ParseError.expected: ExpectedSet` (a `BTreeSet<&'static str>`) collects every literal/`expected!()` that failed at the furthest position; Display prints 'expected one of ...'.

custom-error-types.comment: Rules always return `Result<T, ParseError<L>>`; only the location type `L` varies with the input. Users convert afterwards via `map_err`.

error-span-fidelity.comment: Guideline 3: a single failure position (`LineCol` with byte offset for str, `usize` for slices); no end position or secondary labels.

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: No optional features or documented bridges to ariadne/miette/codespan/annotate-snippets.

contextual-error-messages.comment: `expected!("text")` injects a human-readable expectation and `quiet!{}` suppresses noisy literals from the expected set; `{? }` actions can fail with a custom `&str`.

incremental-reparsing.comment: Whole-input parse per call; no tree reuse.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Output is whatever the user's actions build; trivia is retained only if the grammar captures it explicitly.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language or highlighting API.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: No rust-analyzer/helix/zed/neovim dependency found among reverse dependencies (checked 2026-09-19).

runtime-speed-tier.comment: epage/parse-benchmarks-rs JSON benchmark (rustc 1.94.1, peg v0.8.5, checked 2026-09-19): 29 ms vs 18 ms for hand-written serde_json (~1.6x) — just over the 1.5x top-tier line; second-fastest library after winnow (27 ms), ahead of lalrpop 40, chumsky 47, pest 62, nom 68. Maintainer-authored (winnow) but includes competitors and is reproducible; 'parsers have not been validated'.

compile-time-impact.comment: Same benchmark: 2 s debug build for the peg JSON parser (winnow 1 s, pest/nom 3 s, chumsky 5 s, lalrpop 12 s). Generated code is plain recursive-descent functions; proc-macro deps are only proc-macro2/quote (no syn).

allocation-strategy.comment: Runtime needs `alloc` (expected set is a `BTreeSet`; `#[cache]` memo tables), so not allocation-free. AST allocation is fully user-controlled in actions; an arena can be threaded in as a grammar argument.

generated-code-size.comment: One Rust function per rule, no parse tables; parse-benchmarks-rs reports 77 KiB binary overhead for the JSON grammar (winnow 67, pest 119, lalrpop 1,523).

no-std-support.comment: Asserted but not CI-tested (Assessment Guideline → null). peg-runtime is `#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]` with `alloc` required (BTreeSet); `std` is a default feature since 0.8.2. CI (rust.yml) only builds stable/1.82 with default features — no `--no-default-features` job — and 0.8.6 notes list a no-std compatibility fix, i.e. it has regressed before.

msrv.comment: Cargo.toml `rust-version = "1.82.0"`; CI pins 1.82.0. Raised from earlier in 0.8.6.

unsafe-usage.comment: No `unsafe` found in peg-runtime (lib.rs, str.rs, slice.rs, error.rs) or peg-macros/lib.rs, but no `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` is declared, so tagged minimal rather than forbid.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: `peg::parser!` is a `proc-macro = true` crate (peg-macros); it is the only way to define a grammar.

build-rs-step.comment: Code generation happens in the proc macro; README contrasts this with lalrpop's build script.

dependency-count.comment: Umbrella crate `peg`: peg-macros + peg-runtime. The runtime crate the binary links against (`peg-runtime`) has zero dependencies; peg-macros (compile-time) pulls proc-macro2 and quote.

wasm-compatible.comment: Inferred: pure Rust, zero-dependency runtime with no platform-specific code; the proc macro runs on the host. No wasm32 CI job verified.

async-friendly.comment: Generated parsers are plain functions over a complete slice; `ParseError<L>` is Send + Sync when `L` is. No streaming, so async input must be fully buffered first.

crates-io-downloads.comment: All-time downloads of `peg`, checked 2026-09-19 (~2.0M/month per lib.rs).

maintenance-status.comment: Release 0.8.6 on 2026-05-04 (within 6 months of 2026-09-19) with a new feature (injected span variables); commits Nov 2025–May 2026; 43 open issues. Release cadence is slow (roughly one release per 8–14 months) but steady since 2014.

documentation-quality.comment: Guideline 3: thorough crate-level grammar reference on docs.rs plus README with a worked example and comparison table; ~38 runnable test grammars serve as examples. No book/tutorial or migration guides beyond release notes; peg-runtime rustdoc coverage 82%.

tutorial-book.comment: Only the rustdoc grammar reference and README; no dedicated long-form guide.

notable-users.value: LibCST (Meta/Instagram Python CST parser), gherkin (cucumber-rs), brush (Bash-compatible shell), jrsonnet
notable-users.comment: Verified via Cargo.toml for LibCST (`peg = "0.8.5"`), gherkin (`peg = "0.6.3"`), brush-parser (`peg = "0.8.6"`); jrsonnet-types/ir listed on lib.rs reverse deps.
